ESB was established in 1927 as a statutory corporation in the Republic of Ireland under the Electricity (Supply) Act 1927. With a holding of approximately 97.1%, ESB is majority owned by the Irish Government. The remaining approximate 2.9% is held by the trustees of an Employee Share Ownership Plan. As a strong, diversified, vertically integrated utility, ESB operates right across the electricity market: from generation, through transmission and distribution, to supply. In addition, ESB extracts further value at certain points along this chain: supplying gas, using our networks to carry fibre for telecommunications, developing electric vehicle public charging infrastructure and more. ESB is a leading Irish utility focused on providing excellent customer service and maintaining our financial strength. We have a regulated asset base of approximately €12 billion with 30% of electricity generation capacity in the all-island market.

STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. entity_geography.text: dio Reading Download (BARD) Wishlist, stream NLS talking books, and manage the patron’s Bookshelf using a voice-only interface available on Alexa-enabled commercial smart-speaker platforms. The contractor shall be responsible for providing RealSAM Dialog licenses and services required to operate the system in production, while meeting all IT information-system security requirements as required by the Library of Congress. C.2 BACKGROUND NLS administers a free program that loans audio and braille books and magazines, music scores in braille and large print, and specially designed audio-playback and refreshable-braille-display equipment to residents of the United States who are unable to read or use standard print materials due to visual or physical impairment. ip_data_security.text: the cost of services needed to operate and maintain NLS’s My Talking Books (an Amazon Alexa skill) in production. My Talking Books is an Amazon Alexa skill that enables NLS patrons to search the NLS collection, browse the NLS collection, retrieve/manage the patron’s Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) Wishlist, stream NLS talking books, and manage the patron’s Bookshelf using a voice-only interface available on Alexa-enabled commercial smart-speaker platforms. The contractor shall be responsible for providing RealSAM Dialog licenses and services required to operate the system in production, while meeting all IT information-system security requirements as required by the Library of Congress. C.2 BACKGROUND NLS administers a free program that loans audio and braille books and magazines, music scores in braille and large print, and specially designed audio-playback and refreshable-braille-display equipment to residents of the United States who are unable to read or use standard print materials due to visual or physical impairment. NLS administers the program nationally, while direct service to eligible individuals and institutions is the responsibility of cooperating network libraries in the various states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the U. S. Virgin Islands. Thi

hall provide the Library with license and technical support. This support shall be provided on an annual basis at a firm-fixed price. This support shall be provided in blocks of 500. This support service must ensure that users with legacy RealSAM Dialog licenses can use the My Talking Books skill in production. The contractor shall provide the Library with a price schedule (Attachment J3 - Pricing Chart.xlsx) for the following scenarios: A. RealSAM Dialog License Support – An annual fee for blocks of 500 perpetual user licenses for the RealSAM dialog engine. This scenario reflects the current state of affairs where the contractor is hosting all required non-GFE services (Auth Proxy, Streaming Servers, Dialog Engine, etc.). B. RealSAM Dialog License Support with Auth Proxy hosted by the Library – same as scenario A, but the Library would host the Auth Proxy service instead of the contractor. C. RealSAM Legacy Dialog License Support with Auth Proxy and Streaming Servers hosted by the Library – same as scenario A, but the Library would host both the Auth Proxy service and Streaming Servers instead of the contractor.
